decision: Coders and the adjudicator see each window with the whole session history before its request, nothing cut: every earlier turn's editor, request, AI response and what happened next, then this window's editor, request, response and next actions. No turn after this window's next actions
why: Bet 4 showed only the last 3 earlier turns, and 10 of its windows reuse text from AI responses in turns nobody saw (coding/REPORT.md). v1.1 s2 and s5 need to know whether supplied text came from an earlier AI turn
effect: The 3-turn limit and the 500-character cap on earlier turns are gone

decision: History is given as one part file per window, read in turn order. A coder labels window k before reading part k+1 of that session. Labels go in only through add_label.py, which refuses a second label for a window, so no label is revised after reading later turns
why: Per-window views with full history total about 3 MB for the 277 windows; one pass per session is about a third of that. The order rule keeps each label to history up to its window
effect: Checked from transcripts by scripts/audit_access.py (order of add_label calls and part reads)

decision: Coders read a coder copy of v1.1 with section 9 (how Q3-Q5 are reported, the risk indicators) removed. The frozen file is not edited; the copy is made by script and records the source's SHA-256
why: The task bars coders from any category or risk mapping. Bet 4 coders read the whole codebook including s9, so this is a difference between the runs
effect: s9 is reporting guidance with no coding rule; sections 1-8 and 10-12 are word for word

decision: Coders label every window of every session in their batch, all 347. Adjudication covers the 277 new windows and the 18 Bet 4 windows in coding/results/older_turns.json (windows_with_unseen_older_turns). The other 52 Bet 4 windows are relabeled only as a side check and not adjudicated
why: A coder reads every turn anyway, and coding each in order keeps the session whole. The older_turns list has 18 windows with unseen turns, 10 of them with reused unseen AI text; all 18 are the sensitivity set
effect: The 52 give a full-view vs Bet 4 comparison where the view hid little

decision: Final-label rule, fixed before any Bet 6 label exists: the 277 new windows take Bet 6 final labels (A=B, else adjudicator, else UNSETTLED, then v1.1 s7 script rule on U1 vs U2). The 18 sensitivity windows also take the Bet 6 full-view final label, whatever it is, with the Bet 4 label kept in bet4_ columns. The other 52 keep Bet 4 final labels
why: The full view shows strictly more of what v1.1 s2 and s5 ask coders to judge, so for the 18 it is the better-informed reading. For the 52 the Bet 4 view already showed all earlier turns and reused cut text
effect: source column says bet6, bet6_fullview_recode or bet4

decision: Same roles and requested models as Bet 4: Coder A opus, Coder B sonnet, adjudicator opus, fresh agents per batch, whole sessions per batch, A and B run in parallel, adjudicator sees first and second with a seeded flip

Agreement is computed by script on the 295 adjudicated windows and on follow-up windows (C1+C2), with window and session-clustered bootstrap intervals, Bet 4's kappa code imported. u4_subtype is never in an agreement claim
